content.value_statement: Taiwan income tax estimates require the correct income year, exemptions, deductions, and progressive tax brackets. This skill provides offline calculations for years 114 and 115 with official references and clear coverage limits.
actual_capabilities: Estimate taxable income and progressive tax for income years 114 and 115 using the included Python function.
Apply personal exemptions, standard deductions, and a salary deduction capped at the published annual limit.
Accept marital status, additional household members, senior counts, other income, and manually supplied additional deductions.
Explain published tax brackets and show the deductions used in an estimate.
Report the income year, official source references, and excluded tax items with each estimate.
Calculate supported years without API keys, login, or network access.
limitations: Only income years 114 and 115 are encoded; other years require checking official announcements before calculation.
The skill does not file returns or determine every deduction eligibility rule.
Itemized deductions, basic living expense differences, dividend tax options, and alternative minimum tax are not modeled.
The function applies one salary deduction cap to the supplied salary total; it does not model separate spouse salary deductions.

use_cases.title: Plan a Salary Budget
use_cases.description: Estimate annual tax from a stated salary and household profile, then identify deductions excluded from the calculation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Household Tax Questions
use_cases.description: Compare simplified estimates using household member counts and standard deductions before consulting a tax professional about omitted rules.

use_cases.title: Explain Progressive Tax Rates
use_cases.description: Use the included examples to demonstrate taxable income, marginal brackets, and differences between supported income years.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate a Single Salary
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate tax for income year 115: single, TWD 800,000 salary, no dependents, and no other income. Show deductions and official sources.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: calculate a simple salary estimate.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Income Years
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare years 114 and 115 for a single person earning TWD 800,000, without dependents or other income. Explain the estimate difference.

prompt_templates.title: Include Household Members
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate year 115 for a single filer with TWD 1,200,000 salary and two eligible dependents, one aged 72. Show assumptions and exclusions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: include household exemptions and a senior.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Complex Estimate
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate year 115 with TWD 2,000,000 salary, TWD 100,000 ordinary other income, and TWD 30,000 verified additional deductions. Assume single, no dependents. Show progressive brackets, assumptions, sources, and omitted rules. Do not determine deduction eligibility.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review multiple inputs and coverage boundaries.

output_examples.input: Estimate year 115 tax for a single person with TWD 800,000 salary and no dependents or other income.
output: Income year: 115, corresponding to 2026 income and filing in May 2027.
Deductions: TWD 101,000 personal exemption, TWD 136,000 standard deduction, and TWD 227,000 salary deduction.
Estimated taxable income: TWD 336,000. Estimated tax at 5%: TWD 16,800.
Source: Ministry of Finance announcement 1140466407, cited through the government Gazette.
Estimate only; other deductions and tax regimes are excluded.

output_examples.input: Compare years 114 and 115 for a single person with TWD 800,000 salary and no dependents or other income.
output: Year 114: estimated taxable income TWD 354,000; estimated tax TWD 17,700.
Year 115: estimated taxable income TWD 336,000; estimated tax TWD 16,800.
The year 115 estimate is TWD 900 lower because the included exemptions and deductions are larger.
Sources: the Ministry of Finance announcement dated 2024-11-28 and announcement 1140466407.
Both calculations use standard deductions and exclude other deductions and tax regimes.

best_practices: Confirm the income year, marital status, household member counts, and income categories before calculating.
Use anonymous financial totals; names, identity numbers, credentials, and tax documents are unnecessary for this calculation.
Check official announcements for unsupported years and label every result as an estimate with explicit exclusions.
anti_patterns: Treating the filing year as the income year or reusing old figures for unsupported years.
Using this simplified model as a complete joint return calculation or a final tax liability.
Including dividends, overseas income, or unverified deductions without explaining that their tax treatment is outside the model.

faq.question: Which income years are supported?
faq.answer: The included figures cover ROC years 114 and 115, corresponding to 2025 and 2026 income.

faq.question: Does the calculation require an API key or internet connection?
faq.answer: No API key or login is required. Supported calculations are offline; checking official sources or unsupported years may require internet access.

faq.question: Can this skill file my tax return?
faq.answer: No. It provides estimates only. Use the official Ministry of Finance filing service for actual returns.

faq.question: How should I count household members?
faq.answer: The function counts the filer automatically. Its dependents input includes the spouse and other eligible members; clarify senior eligibility separately.

faq.question: Can I include additional deductions?
faq.answer: You can supply a verified total through extra_deduction. The function does not validate eligibility or calculate those deductions.

faq.question: Does it handle all household income and tax rules?
faq.answer: No. Separate spouse salary deductions, itemized deductions, basic living expense differences, dividend options, and alternative minimum tax require separate assessment.
